clue.text: Finally redeployed an old falconer

indicators.note: to redeploy is to rearrange or move to new positions, so these letters are set out afresh

explanation.surface: An elderly falconer has been given a new posting, at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally' looks like a scene-setting adverb but is the definition; 'redeployed' shuffles all thirteen letters of AN OLD FALCONER.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means conclusively, once and never again, which is what 'finally' means in 'settled finally'.

clue.text: Counterpart stupidly bit me on purpose

indicators.note: stupidly suggests something done foolishly and out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone complains that their rival bit them deliberately.
explanation.definitionFit: Your opposite number is the person holding the equivalent role on the other side, your counterpart.

clue.text: Domestic pet about to return, so put food out?

parts.note: a cat is a common household pet

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the two letters for about are read backwards

parts.note: re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Feeding the cat on its return home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put food out' looks like feeding the pet; the question mark marks the definition as loose: to cater is to supply food.
explanation.definitionFit: To cater is to provide food and drink, as for a party.

clue.text: Open over committee

parts.note: above means over
a board is a committee governing an organisation

explanation.surface: Something openly placed before a committee.
explanation.definitionFit: Dealings that are above board are honest and open, nothing concealed.

clue.text: Cover up girl's problem that seems incapable of a solution

definitions.text: problem that seems incapable of a solution

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for cover is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a lid is a cover
Emma is a girl's name; the 's is read as 'is', joining it to the definition

explanation.surface: A girl's awkward problem in hushing something up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover up' reads as concealing, but splits: 'up' is the reversal signal, since in a down clue the word reads upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilemma is a situation with only unwelcome choices, so no clean solution.

clue.text: Male rowers, dreadful moaners

indicators.note: dreadful suggests something in a terrible mess, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A crew of men in a boat who complain dreadfully.
explanation.definitionFit: Oarsmen are people who row a boat, men by the word's form.

clue.text: Song, one from 'West Side Story' needing no introduction

indicators.note: with no introduction the opening letter of the character's name is dropped

parts.note: Maria is the heroine of the musical West Side Story

explanation.surface: A famous song from West Side Story needing no introduction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing no introduction' reads as praise for a famous song but drops the first letter of MARIA.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is a solo song, chiefly in opera.

clue.text: Listen and learn, unhappily, about European

indicators.note: about means around, so the jumbled letters go round the abbreviation
unhappily implies things going badly, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to a reluctant pupil to listen and learn about Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unhappily' rearranges AND LEARN to LNDANAR spread around E.
explanation.definitionFit: To lend an ear is to listen attentively to someone.

clue.text: Tense show, faultless

parts.note: to present is to show
perfect means faultless

explanation.surface: A nervous but flawless performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' looks like nervous, but it is the grammatical tense.
explanation.definitionFit: The present perfect is a verb tense, as in 'I have eaten'.

clue.text: Work of little merit in vessel, British tanker

parts.note: a pot is a cooking vessel
an oiler is a ship that carries oil, a tanker

explanation.surface: A sneer at some poor piece of writing about a British oil ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A potboiler is a book or artwork churned out just to earn money, so of little artistic merit.

clue.text: Private meal missed by daughter

indicators.note: something missed by the meal is absent from it, so the daughter's letter is dropped from that word

parts.note: dinner is a meal

explanation.surface: A family dinner held privately, which the daughter failed to attend.
explanation.definitionFit: Inner thoughts or feelings are private ones, kept within rather than shown.

clue.text: Fling? Witness pair inside

indicators.note: inside places the abbreviation for pair within the word for witness

parts.note: to witness is to see

explanation.surface: A tabloid hint of an affair: a fling, with a couple caught in the act by a witness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fling' suggests an affair, but here it is a burst of indulgence; the question mark flags the shift in sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A fling is a short spell of wild enjoyment, as is a spending or drinking spree.

clue.text: I am contracted in Maine to produce a type of theatrical drama

indicators.note: in puts the shortened form of 'I am' within the state's abbreviation

parts.note: ME is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Maine
'I am' shortened is I'M

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of a contract to stage a show in Maine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contracted' looks like signing a deal but means shortened, giving I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: Mime is a form of theatre performed through gesture and movement without words.

clue.text: Just like in outskirts of Paris, while away

indicators.note: in puts the two-letter word for 'just like' between the Paris border letters
outskirts are the edges of a town, so only the first and last letters of Paris are used

parts.note: as means just like, as in 'as good as new'

explanation.surface: Spending idle time on the edge of Paris, just like a tourist.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass the time is to while it away, spending hours idly.

clue.text: Batting: sound job, to a great extent

parts.note: a cricket batter who is batting is said to be in
good means sound, as in a good investment
a part is a role or job someone has

explanation.surface: A cricket report praising a batter who has done a sound job for much of the innings.
explanation.definitionFit: In good part can mean largely, for the most part, as well as good-humouredly.

clue.text: Draw hat picked up by cat

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

indicators.note: picked up means heard, as a radio picks up a signal, so the hat's name is given by its sound

parts.note: a bowler is a round hard felt hat

explanation.surface: A cat collecting a fallen hat, perhaps in a cartoon sketch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw' suggests sketching, but it is a prize draw; BOLA is spelt to sound like the bowler hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A tombola is a lottery in which tickets are pulled from a revolving drum, a kind of prize draw.

clue.text: Timid type, prior to gin and Cheddar cheese

indicators.note: prior to means coming before, so the timid type is placed before the gin

parts.note: a timid person is often called a mouse
a gin is a snare or trap for animals

explanation.surface: A shy person having a drink before a cheese course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gin' is not the drink but a snare. Mousetrap is British slang for cheap, ordinary Cheddar.
explanation.definitionFit: Mousetrap is a jokey British name for plain cheese, cheap Cheddar fit only to bait a trap.

clue.text: Gran eager to find a hard-wearing fabric

parts.note: nan is an informal word for grandmother, as gran is
keen means eager

explanation.surface: Grandma shopping for sturdy cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Nankeen is a durable yellowish cotton cloth, originally made in Nanjing.

clue.text: Indifferent as late run failed?

indicators.note: a run that failed has gone wrong, so its letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A shrug at a sporting effort: a late run that came to nothing leaves one unmoved.
explanation.definitionFit: Being neutral means taking no side, being indifferent to who wins.

clue.text: Soundly beat husband after wager in London borough

indicators.note: after means the husband's letter follows the wager

parts.note: to lam is to thrash soundly
a bet is a wager

explanation.surface: A wife thrashing her husband after a bet in a London district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soundly' is not a sound-alike signal: 'soundly beat' together means thrash, LAM. Lambeth is a London borough south of the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambeth is an inner London borough, home of Lambeth Palace.

clue.text: She finally received rent, a personal morale-booster

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word She

parts.note: got means received
a rent is a tear, a rip

explanation.surface: A landlady cheered at last to receive the rent she was owed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' looks like money paid but is a tear in cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: An ego trip is something done mainly for self-gratification, boosting one's own sense of importance.

clue.text: Badminton competitor, say, in uniform — abbreviated name

parts.note: even means uniform, regular

indicators.note: abbreviated means shortened, so the final letter of the word for name is cut

parts.note: a term is a name for something

explanation.surface: A badminton player in team kit, with a shortened name on the shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: Badminton is not the racket sport but the Badminton Horse Trials, a famous English equestrian event.
explanation.definitionFit: An eventer is a horse or rider competing in three-day eventing, such as the Badminton Horse Trials.

clue.text: Look shabby, so they say

indicators.note: so they say signals a word as heard spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: mean can describe something shabby or poor, as in a mean dwelling

explanation.surface: Gossip that someone looks shabby.
explanation.definitionFit: Mien is a person's bearing or appearance, their look.

clue.text: Small mostly submissive Barrie character

indicators.note: mostly means all but the final letter of the word for submissive is kept

parts.note: meek means submissive

explanation.surface: A description of a little, docile figure from J. M. Barrie's work.
explanation.definitionFit: Smee is Captain Hook's bosun in J. M. Barrie's Peter Pan.

clue.text: To put off, in crude terms

indicators.note: in signals the letters are found inside the words crude terms, across the word gap

explanation.surface: Someone discouraged by coarse language.
explanation.definitionFit: To deter is to discourage someone from acting, to put them off.

clue.text: Part of in-depth ingenious article

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A section of a thorough, clever piece of journalism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' looks like a newspaper piece, but means an object.
explanation.definitionFit: An article is an item or object, any thing in general.

clue.text: In France, eat processed cheese

parts.note: F is the international vehicle code for France

indicators.note: processed means treated and changed, so the letters of eat are rearranged

explanation.surface: In France, people eat processed cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Feta is a white brined Greek cheese made from sheep's or goat's milk.

clue.text: Strangely frightening eastern lake

parts.note: Erie is one of the Great Lakes of North America

explanation.surface: A spooky body of water in the east.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie describes something uncanny that inspires a strange fear.

clue.text: Bit player facing season in additional play

indicators.note: facing means standing in front of, so the bit player comes before the season

parts.note: an extra is an actor with a tiny non-speaking part
a season is a period, a time

explanation.surface: A minor actor up against a whole season's demands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' suggests theatre beside the bit player, but it means sport: extra time is added to a drawn match, especially in football.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra time is a further period of play added when a match is level at full time.

clue.text: Pretend one's not interested in baffling drama?

definitions.meaning: feign reluctance, especially to a would-be suitor
a drama, or play, that is difficult to grasp, read whimsically as a stage piece that is hard to understand

explanation.surface: Feigning boredom while watching a puzzling stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase: PLAY is the drama and HARD TO GET means baffling; the question mark marks the whimsy.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means acting coy or uninterested to make oneself more desirable.
